title: One digest per transmission scenario

blocks.text: A transmission planner keeps every scenario's inputs in a dict such as
where `force_in` is a Python set of line ids. Each scenario is named by the sha256 digest of its inputs, so a rerun can prove it used exactly the same ones.

Write `snapshot_digest(inputs)` that returns the 64-character hex digest. Equal inputs must give the same digest whatever order their dicts were built in and in any Python process; a changed number or string, or an item added to or removed from a list or set, must give a different digest. Inputs hold dicts with string keys, lists, sets of strings, strings and numbers, nested to any depth.

The canonical form, as in the lesson, is JSON with sorted keys and each set written as its sorted list. That form does not tell every pair of inputs apart, and the tests don't ask it to: a set and a list holding the same items in sorted order give the same digest, and so would a dict keyed by the number 2027 and one keyed by the string `"2027"`, since JSON writes every key as a string. That is why keys must be strings and a field must always hold the same kind of value.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from scenario import snapshot_digest

inputs = {"budget": {"2031": 5100, "2032": 4800}, "force_in": {"P-3", "P-8", "P-1"},
          "settings": {"seed": 9, "solver": "highs"}}
rebuilt = {"settings": {"solver": "highs", "seed": 9}, "force_in": {"P-1", "P-3", "P-8"},
           "budget": {"2032": 4800, "2031": 5100}}

print("digest of the inputs:", snapshot_digest(inputs))
print("digest, same inputs built in another order:", snapshot_digest(rebuilt))
print("digest, 2032 budget 4700:", snapshot_digest({**inputs, "budget": {"2031": 5100, "2032": 4700}}))

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json


def snapshot_digest(inputs: dict) -> str:
    """sha256 hex digest of the inputs, the same for equal inputs in every process."""
    # TODO: write it.
    return "0" * 64


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(snapshot_digest({"budget": {"2027": 4200}, "force_in": {"T-07", "T-11"}, "gap": 0.0}))
